5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 5

Adverbs of frequency

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Say how often we do things (con qué frecuencia)
  • Learn always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely and never
  • Put the adverb in the right place in the sentence
  • Ask and answer How often…? with once, twice and every

Para pensar

¿Te lavas los dientes todos los días? ¿Comes brócoli de vez en cuando? ¿Has subido a un camello alguna vez? ¿Cómo dirías en inglés con qué frecuencia haces algo?

Explicación

How often?

Adverbs of frequency tell us how often something happens. We use them with the present simple to talk about routines and habits: «I always have breakfast at eight.» «My cat never drinks milk.» «We sometimes go to the cinema.»

Imagine a scale from 100% to 0%. At the top is always, the thing you do every single time. At the bottom is never, the thing you don't do at all. In the middle there are other words. En castellano: son palabras como «siempre», «a menudo» o «nunca».

Six adverbs

Let's learn them with examples. always (siempre, 100%): «I always wear a seatbelt in the car.» usually (normalmente, 80%): «I usually walk to school.» often (a menudo, 60%): «We often play basketball at break.»

sometimes (a veces, 40%): «My dad sometimes cooks pizza.» rarely or hardly ever (casi nunca, 10%): «I rarely watch the news.» never (nunca, 0%): «Penguins never fly.» Pronunciación: often se dice «ófen» (la t casi no suena) y usually, «iúshuali».

Where does the adverb go?

The position is important. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: «I always get up at seven.» «She often reads comics.» «They never eat meat.»

But with the verb to be, they go after it: «I am always hungry after PE.» «My brother is never late.» «We are usually tired on Fridays.» Truco: «antes del verbo de acción, después de be». En castellano tenemos más libertad, por eso es un error típico.

Sometimes and negatives

Sometimes is special: it can also go at the beginning or the end of the sentence. «Sometimes I go by bike.» «I go by bike sometimes.»

Never is already negative, so we don't use don't with it. ✔ «I never eat sweets at night.» ✘ «I don't never eat…». In negative sentences we can use don't usually or don't often: «I don't usually drink coffee» (normalmente no tomo café). En castellano: decimos «no como nunca», pero en inglés solo hay una negación.

Questions: How often…?

To ask about frequency we say How often…? + do/does: «How often do you go swimming?» «How often does your sister play the violin?»

We can answer with an adverb: «I sometimes go swimming.» Or with an expression of frequency: «Once a week» (una vez a la semana). «Twice a month» (dos veces al mes). «Three times a year» (tres veces al año). «Every day» (todos los días). «Every Saturday».

Once, twice, every…

Expressions of frequency are more exact than adverbs. once = one time; twice = two times; then three times, four times… + a day / a week / a month / a year.

We can also use every: every day, every morning, every weekend, every summer. These expressions usually go at the end of the sentence: «I have English three times a week.» «We visit my aunt every Christmas.» «I go to the dentist twice a year.»

Healthy routines

Adverbs of frequency are perfect to talk about habits. Are your habits healthy? «I always wash my hands before lunch.» «I usually sleep nine or ten hours.» «I often eat fruit.» «I sometimes eat chips.» «I rarely drink fizzy drinks.» «I never go to bed after eleven.»

Look at your week. Is there something you want to do more often? Something you want to do less often? Writing your routine in English helps you practise and think about your health at the same time.

Reading: a busy family

Read Joel's text: «My family is very busy. My mum is a nurse, so she often works at night. My dad always makes breakfast and takes us to school. My sister Clara plays the trumpet. She practises every day, and our neighbours are sometimes angry! I play football twice a week. On Sundays we usually visit my grandparents. We never watch TV at lunch because we talk. We rarely eat out, but once a month we have a pizza night.»

How often does Joel play football? Who always makes breakfast? What do they never do?

Let's practise: class survey

Make a class survey. Prepare five questions with How often…?: «How often do you read a book?», «How often do you eat vegetables?», «How often do you play video games?» Ask five classmates and write their answers in a table.

Then report the results: «Three people always eat vegetables. Two people rarely read books. Everybody plays video games sometimes!» Repaso: el adverbio va antes del verbo y después de be; never no lleva don't; las expresiones como twice a week van al final.

Adverbs of frequency

Ejercicios

  1. Order from 100% to 0%: sometimes, never, always, often, usually, rarely.

  2. Put the adverb in place: «We go to the park.» (often)

  3. Put the adverb in place: «They are noisy.» (sometimes)

  4. Correct: «He watches never TV.»

  5. Translate: «Normalmente desayuno cereales.»

  6. Write in English: «una vez al mes».

  7. Make the question: «___ ___ do you play tennis?» — «Once a week.»

  8. Correct: «I don't never eat fish.»

  9. Write a sentence with «every Sunday».

  10. Write four sentences about your routine with four different adverbs.

Practica

  1. «Always» means…

    1. A) nunca
    2. B) a veces
    3. C) siempre

  2. «Never» means…

    1. A) nunca
    2. B) a menudo
    3. C) casi siempre

  3. Which adverb is about 40%?

    1. A) usually
    2. B) sometimes
    3. C) always

  4. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) I walk usually to school.
    2. B) I usually walk to school.
    3. C) Usually I walk usually.

  5. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) She often is tired.
    2. B) Often she tired.
    3. C) She is often tired.

  6. «___ do you go swimming?» — «Twice a week.»

    1. A) How often
    2. B) How many
    3. C) When often

  7. «Twice» means…

    1. A) one time
    2. B) every time
    3. C) two times

  8. «I ___ eat meat.» (vegetarian)

    1. A) don't never
    2. B) never
    3. C) always

  9. «Rarely» is similar to…

    1. A) hardly ever
    2. B) usually
    3. C) often

  10. «He ___ plays chess.»

    1. A) sometimes
    2. B) sometime
    3. C) some times

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué son los adverbios de frecuencia y su escala; Dónde se colocan en la frase con un verbo de acción y con to be; Por qué never no lleva don't; Cómo se pregunta y se responde con How often.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

alwaysSiempre (100 %).
usuallyNormalmente.
oftenA menudo.
sometimesA veces.
rarely / hardly everCasi nunca.
neverNunca (sin don't).
How often…?¿Con qué frecuencia…?
once / twiceUna vez / dos veces.

Soluciones

  1. C) 100 %.
  2. A) 0 %.
  3. B) A veces.
  4. B) Antes del verbo.
  5. C) Con be, después.
  6. A) Pregunta de frecuencia.
  7. C) Dos veces.
  8. B) Never sin don't.
  9. A) Casi nunca.
  10. A) Sometimes, junto.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never.
  2. We often go to the park.
  3. They are sometimes noisy. (También: Sometimes they are noisy.)
  4. He never watches TV.
  5. I usually have cereal for breakfast.
  6. once a month.
  7. How often.
  8. I never eat fish.
  9. Model answer: We visit my grandma every Sunday.
  10. Model answer: I always brush my teeth. I usually walk to school. I sometimes read comics. I never eat chips for breakfast.
